questions.solution_html:
• Examine the bias and data-privacy concerns and suggest suitable responsible AI measures. Suggested
  • allocation: 5 marks.
  • Suggested pointers for the answer: (1 mark may be awarded to identification and explanation
  • per point)
  • Bias concern: regional languages are inadequately represented in training data, causing different
  • chatbot performance and unequal service across customer groups.
  • Privacy concern: customers are not clearly informed about use of purchase histories and conversations,
  • weakening transparency and meaningful control over their data.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of Artificial Narrow Intelligence? / [CO1] a). A machine capable of performing every intellectual task like a human b). A hypothetical machine more intelligent than humans in all fields c). A chatbot designed to answer customer enquiries d). A computer without specialised software
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how collaboration can support introduction of the system while preserving employee roles and
  • managerial accountability. Suggested allocation: 5 marks.
  • Complementary roles: AI forecasts stock requirements, answers routine enquiries and analyses records;
  • employees contribute judgement, customer understanding and contextual knowledge.
  • Human review and authority: managers check important recommendations, such as stock orders, and
  • can approve, modify or reject them. Complex chatbot issues are escalated to staff.
  • Training and employee participation: provide AI literacy and practical training; involve employees in
  • the pilot, redesign work with them and explain how their roles will develop.
  • Clear accountability: assign named managers or teams to validate outputs, approve consequential
  • decisions, investigate errors and remain answerable for outcomes.
  • Continuous feedback and monitoring: staff report incorrect forecasts, chatbot errors and language
  • issues; the company reviews outcomes, records decisions and improves the system.
  • Any other criterion identified in the case. Criteria need not be given a heading. One mark may be allocated to
  • each point identified in the answer.
  • Note that this is an Apply-based case study. Hence, marks may be awarded if students have been able to
  • successfully defend the answers based on the case study and additional knowledge about the topic. Mark
  • liberally.

questions.question: Sahaya Mart's AI Transformation Sahaya Mart, a growing Indian retail chain, plans to introduce an AI system across its physical stores and online platform. The proposed system will study purchase records to forecast stock requirements, assist customers through a chatbot and help store managers make faster operational decisions. The management expects the project to reduce stock-outs, improve customer service and support business growth. A pilot study, however, reveals several concerns. Customer records contain missing entries, duplicate profiles and outdated contact details. Some stores have reliable internet connectivity and modern systems, while others use older computers. Employees fear that the technology may replace their jobs, and many managers have limited knowledge of AI. The company has not yet clearly assigned responsibility for checking AI-generated decisions. The pilot chatbot also performs differently across customer groups because its training data does not adequately represent all regional languages. Customers are not clearly informed about how their purchase histories and conversations will be used. Sahaya Mart therefore decides that employees must review important AI decisions, customers must receive clear information about data use, and staff must be trained to work effectively with the new system. Answer the following questions based on the case study: 1. Identify the major challenges that Sahaya Mart may face while implementing AI. Support your answer with evidence from the case. 2. Examine the bias and data-privacy concerns in the proposed AI system. Suggest suitable responsible AI measures. 3. Explain how human-AI collaboration can help Sahaya Mart introduce the system without weakening employee roles or managerial accountability. / [CO2] [15x1 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
Step-by-Step Valuation Scheme:
1. Theoretical Framework & Assumptions (2.0 Marks): Statement of foundational premises, variables, and starting conditions.
2. Analytical Development & Proof Steps (2.0 Marks): Rigorous derivation, systematic reasoning, and logical progression.
3. Synthesized Conclusion & Interpretation (2.0 Marks): Final formulated result, physical/academic significance, and domain limitations.
Model Solution: Provide structured answers with numbered points or labeled steps. Ensure all intermediate calculations or logical assertions are fully supported with standard university academic rigor.
